_comment: The todo graph. A TODO is a PERSON's outstanding item — the human half of memory. It is NOT a second work plan: `beans/` is the agent work plan and `AGENTS.md` forbids standing another up beside it. The two sit in different quadrants of one 2x2 — memory against workflow management, human against agent — and conflating them is the drift this repo keeps paying for. A human's memory is a todo; an agent's is `memory/`; an agent's workflow management is `beans/`; and human workflow management is EMPTY, deliberately and still. Two nodes rather than one because the difference is real: an `items` todo is raised about anything, a `feedback` todo against a specific block with the submitter's identity — the same split as `bean-defs` against `workflow-state`. Paths resolve against THIS file's directory, the rule `beans/beans.json` follows, so the whole graph relocates by moving one folder. Schema: schemas/todo-graph.ts; the node shape is schemas/todo.ts.
name: folio-assistant
_defaultTheme_comment: The theme a todo takes when it does not choose one. `grumpy-cat` is THIS INSTANCE'S OWN — the theme `cat-harness/harness.json` gives its own landing card — and that is the whole reason it is safe as a default. Owner, bean `5y4b`: themes are assigned "based on content", "used jugement", and a judgement is a CLAIM about the todo. `operations` on a todo that is nothing of the sort says something false; the instance's own theme says only "this belongs to this folio", which is true of every todo here. So the default makes no claim and a per-todo override makes one deliberately. Declared here rather than in the generator because a folio's own theme is the folio's to choose, and a literal in shared code would be this repository's answer imposed on every downstream instance.

directories.description: One Markdown file per todo, carrying `$schema: folio-todo/v1` in its front matter. Tagged against the knowledge graph — roles, processes, tasks, identities, references and artefacts — so "what is outstanding here" is answerable from any node.
Todos raised against a specific block, carrying the submitter's identity. The content-review feedback workflow the `todo-review` skill reads.
